Search Quality Benchmark

Open-source search engines. Public datasets. Quality first.
Compare full-text, vector, and hybrid search across open-source engines and public datasets. Relevance is the primary measure; latency and throughput provide additional context.

Methodology ↗
DATASET EXPLORER
QUALITYComparison metricApplies to all quality views below.

Overall quality

Mean relative shows average quality across the selected dataset/query-set cohorts. Quality floor shows the engine’s worst relative result: how close it stays to the best observed result even on its weakest cohort. Engines missing a selected cohort remain visible but are not ranked.

Reference values are computed from all benchmarked engines for the selected datasets and modes, including engines currently hidden by the engine filter. Higher is better for both Mean relative and Quality floor.

Quality consistency across datasets

Each small dot is one selected dataset, normalized to the best observed result on that dataset. The ring marks the engine’s weakest dataset (Quality floor); the diamond marks Mean relative. A tight cluster near 100% means consistently strong quality without large workload-specific drops. Engines with partial coverage are labeled with their dataset count and use a hollow mean marker.

Dataset Quality floor Mean relative

Quality × latency

Use latency to understand the cost of search quality on this dataset. Performance is supporting context only and does not affect benchmark ranking.

Performance note. This benchmark is designed primarily to compare search quality. Latency and QPS were measured with a lightweight methodology and may be noisy; use them only as directional context, not as an authoritative performance comparison.
QPS is the observed query rate at concurrency 1 and should not be read as maximum throughput.

Dataset × engine quality matrix

Each cell uses the best result among the selected search modes for one dataset/query-set cohort. TREC-COVID appears once per official topic field (query, question, narrative); distinct short and long query sets are separate columns, and identical texts share one “same text” cohort. “Per-dataset relative” is the engine score divided by the best observed score in that cohort. Color uses a fixed scale, so the same percentage always has the same color across filters and screenshots.

<90%100%

Search mode comparison

Compares Full-text, Vector, and Hybrid on one normalized cross-dataset scale. Each point is that engine/mode’s mean per-dataset quality relative to the best observed result in the same dataset. Lines connect the modes in the order Full-text → Vector → Hybrid.

Full-text Vector Hybrid
Filled markers have complete coverage for the selected datasets. Hollow markers are partial and include their coverage in the tooltip.

Latency shape

The three points show typical latency (P50), slower requests (P95), and tail latency (P99). A short line means consistent response times. The horizontal scale is logarithmic; lower is better.

Performance note. This benchmark is designed primarily to compare search quality. Latency and QPS were measured with a lightweight methodology and may be noisy; use them only as directional context, not as an authoritative performance comparison.

Eight independent slowest successful query samples from every run matching the focused dataset, engine and search-mode filters, ordered by latency.
